title: Production scheduler fairness primitives: WorkItem, ring, resource, opportunity-evidence and cap-revision contracts
description:
Objective: land the production scheduler fairness primitives — WorkItem, ring, resource, opportunity-evidence and cap-revision contracts — under packages/scheduler/src/fairness/**, so that task-10cab3e5 (Fair scheduler production) has a real subject to implement against instead of a DEVELOPMENT_ONLY reference that excludes the very structures it needs.

CREATED BY governor-f70d1157 at human direction on 2026-08-10, to the SPECIFICATION WRITTEN BY governor-42b952c9 in their audit comment on task-10cab3e5. That audit is the authority for this task's shape; read it. A governor created this task; an ARCHITECT must plan it. Nothing below is a plan.

WHY THIS EXISTS — IT IS THE ONLY THING THAT CAN CLEAR A PERMANENT DEAD END. governor-42b952c9's audit states it plainly: "THIS BLOCK CAN NEVER CLEAR ON ITS OWN... the condition that would satisfy this block has no owner and no existence. That makes this a PERMANENT DEAD END by construction, not a task that is merely waiting." The remedy was routed to #architects on 2026-08-09, the channel had hit its chat loop guard and returned routingTargets: [] so nobody was notified, and the fleet went down before it was re-routed. architect-8c9073cd, who was to author it, is no longer registered.

BLAST RADIUS — five tasks, the entire expansion tail of epic-e0c54bddb, queue behind this: task-10cab3e5 (Fair scheduler production), task-005c9896 (Expansion admission protocol), task-2561a780 (Scheduler expansion admission), task-b863bae8 (Expansion manual approval binding), task-a1e7f75e (Expansion protocol public hardening). Two more sit behind those: task-cda6bddf (Same-bug circuit breaker) and task-dddfaf83 (Graph supersession engine).

MEASURED ON DISK by governor-f70d1157 at 06:35Z on 2026-08-10, independently of the audit. Verify every line before trusting it:
- There is NO WDRR, ring, deficit-round or resource-queue production code anywhere under packages/scheduler/src. The directory holds admission/, authority/, budget/, convergence/, dependencies/, frontier, graph analysis and determinism modules — and nothing implementing fairness rotation.
- packages/scheduler/src/fairness/ DOES NOT EXIST. This task creates it.
- The reference model is docs/plans/2026-08-07-fable-fairness-aging-reference.md, banner line 1: "DEVELOPMENT_ONLY / NOT_CONFIRMATORY". Its executable form lives in packages/testkit/src/scheduler-fairness/ — fairness-model.ts, fairness-codec.ts, fairness-lifecycle.ts, fairness-internal.ts, fairness-input.ts and their tests.
- Commit d33240c ("fix: harden fairness reference contracts") is the only correction candidate and carries no independent closure artifact.

THE CENTRAL CONSTRAINT — DO NOT DERIVE THE CONTRACTS FROM THE REFERENCE MODEL. The block on task-10cab3e5 is explicit that the landed DEVELOPMENT_ONLY reference EXCLUDES the WDRR rings and resource queues, trusts caller-declared bypass IDs, and retains hostile-state gaps. Copying it forward would import those gaps into production and is the Clause 2 failure both governors named. Measure the gap SYMBOL BY SYMBOL ON DISK and design the production contracts to close it; consult the reference for vocabulary and counterexamples, never as the source of authority.

NOT IN SCOPE, and this list is binding: implementing the WDRR rotation algorithm itself or the aging policy (that is task-10cab3e5, which consumes these contracts); provider launch; graph mutation; changing fairness constants (task-10cab3e5's own rail forbids that without approval, and it applies here too); modifying packages/testkit/src/scheduler-fairness/** — the DEVELOPMENT_ONLY reference stays as it is and is not promoted to production.

THIS TASK SHIPS CONTRACTS, NOT A SCHEDULER. If you find yourself implementing rotation, deficit accounting or aging decisions, you have crossed into task-10cab3e5's scope.

Per Clause 1, name task-10cab3e5 as the consumer in the plan and record its id.

No observation reference accompanies either, so an unclassifiable input is silently admitted as truth. This is the family for typed UNKNOWN naming the missing input.

BRIDGE RULE re-measured, and the plan's counts are off by one in two places: admission 6ts/6js, budget 5/5, convergence 3/3, dependencies 3/3, but authority 8ts/7js and readiness 7ts/6js. implementationPlan.description:
DESIGN THE FIVE FAMILIES FROM THE GAP (read-only). Read the DEVELOPMENT_ONLY reference for VOCABULARY AND COUNTEREXAMPLES ONLY; copying its shapes forward imports its defects, which is the Clause 2 failure two governors independently named.

What the reference legitimately supplies as vocabulary (packages/testkit/src/scheduler-fairness/fairness-model.ts): FairnessPriority "P0"|"P1"|"P2"|"P3"; FairnessTicket; FairnessState; the event union AdmitEvent / CompatibleDispatchEvent / LoseDispatchabilityEvent / RegainDispatchabilityEvent / TerminateEvent / RaiseCapEvent; CapMigration; FairnessIssue / FairnessOk / FairnessError / FairnessResult; SelectedTicket; FairnessBound; and a 12-member FairnessReasonCode union (FAIRNESS_MALFORMED_EVENT, _MALFORMED_STATE, _DUPLICATE_TICKET, _UNKNOWN_TICKET, _STALE_EVENT, _INVALID_PRIORITY, _DISPATCH_ORDER_VIOLATION, _DIMENSION_MISMATCH, _EVENT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, _PROJECT_CEILING_EXCEEDED, _TICKET_CAP_EXCEEDED, CAP_RAISE_REQUIRES_DRAIN_OR_TIGHTER_MIGRATION).

Plan THREE modules under packages/scheduler/src/fairness/, grouped so coupled families share a file and each stays under 250 physical lines:
  fairness-contract.ts   - shared frozen reason-code + refusing-layer vocabularies, and the WorkItem family
  fairness-ring.ts       - the ring family and the resource family (a WDRR ring holds per-resource queues; splitting them across files would force a circular import)
  fairness-evidence.ts    - the opportunity-evidence family and the cap-revision family

Each family is IMMUTABLE TYPES + FROZEN VOCABULARIES + TOTAL VALIDATORS. Freeze every exported array/object with Object.freeze and mark every field readonly.

JUSTIFY EACH SHAPE IN YOUR COMPLETION EVIDENCE against the disk measurement, per DoD 1 — say what the reference lacked and why your shape closes it. "It matches the reference" is the one justification that is not allowed.

If a family genuinely will not fit under 400 lines, SPLIT IT INTO A FOURTH MODULE and say so. The plan-shape file cap binds my submission, not your per-file obligation; a per-file split is always the correct response to an oversized source.
implementationPlan.note:
DESIGN OF THE FIVE FAMILIES, each justified against the disk measurement rather than against the reference. Consumer per Clause 1: task-10cab3e5 (Fair scheduler production).

THE ONE STRUCTURAL DECISION THAT DRIVES ALL FIVE: the production contracts compose this package's already-hardened input kernel (src/runtime-shape.ts + authority/authority-kernel.ts: isPlainRecord, readOwnDataProperty, hasOnlyOwnStringKeys, exactRecord, readList, isCount, oneOf, MAX_AUTHORITY_ITEMS) and this package's identity validator (graph-key.ts isGraphKey). The reference REIMPLEMENTED that kernel in fairness-input.ts with a weaker identity rule. So the contracts are not derived from the reference at all -- they are derived from the scheduler package's own refusal primitives, which is why no new constant is needed and why the identity gap closes for free.

THREE-ARM RESULT, the shape the reference could not express. FairnessContractResult<T> has ok:true | {ok:false, disposition:"REFUSED"} | {ok:false, disposition:"UNKNOWN"}. The reference has exactly two arms (FairnessOk | FairnessError, fairness-model.ts:135-145), so it has NOWHERE to put "structurally legal but unclassifiable" and must either admit it or call it malformed. Every issue carries {code, layer, message, missingInput, subjects}; UNKNOWN issues must carry a non-null missingInput, asserted as a property.

REFUSING-LAYER VOCABULARY, absent from the reference entirely: FairnessIssue is {code, message, ticketIds} -- nothing says WHICH layer refused, so epic rail 6's second clause is unsatisfiable against it. Production adds a frozen closed union FAIRNESS_CONTRACT_LAYERS = WORK_ITEM | RING | RESOURCE | OPPORTUNITY_EVIDENCE | CAP_REVISION and every refusal names one.

FAMILY 1 -- WorkItem (fairness-contract.ts). Shape: {workItemId, dimensionId, priority, resourceId, dispatchability:{state, observationRef: string|null}}.
 - `resourceId` exists because FairnessTicket has no resource field at all; a WDRR ring cannot place an item without knowing which resource queue it belongs to. That is gap (b) reaching back into family 1.
 - `dispatchability.observationRef` is the closure for gap (c). FairnessTicket.dispatchable is a bare boolean documented "Caller-confirmed continuous dispatchability now" -- an unbacked assertion admitted as truth. Production requires the observation reference; `null` is representable and yields UNKNOWN naming `dispatchability.observationRef`, never an optimistic admit.
 - No aging fields (bypassesInLevel, forced, forcedCohortEntryEvent, continuousEligibilityEvent) -- those are aging STATE and aging belongs to task-10cab3e5. Their absence is deliberate, not an omission.

FAMILIES 2+3 -- ring and resource (fairness-ring.ts), designed from a measured void; the reference has no such vocabulary. FairnessRing {ringId, dimensionId, resources: FairnessRingResource[], entries: FairnessRingQueueEntry[]}; FairnessRingResource {resourceId, weight}; FairnessRingQueueEntry {workItemId, resourceId, deficitCounter}. weight and deficitCounter are DATA the contract validates and never computes. Structural invariants, one code each: entry names an undeclared resource; the same workItemId in two different resource queues; a duplicate (workItemId,resourceId) pair; a negative or non-safe-integer counter/weight; an empty resource set while entries exist; duplicate resourceId. The validator does NOT sort resources or entries -- unlike authority/resource-model.ts parseReserveRequest which sorts declaredResources -- precisely so no ordering can be read out of the contract. Caller order is preserved verbatim.

FAMILY 4 -- opportunity evidence (fairness-evidence.ts), the by-construction closure of defect (a). The reference decodes `bypassesInLevel` and range-checks it (fairness-codec.ts:83-84). Production models a bypass as a CLAIM THAT CARRIES ITS PROOF: FairnessBypassClaim {workItemId, claimedBypasses, attestations: FairnessOpportunityAttestation[]}, attestation {opportunityRef, winnerWorkItemId, observationRef: string|null}. validateBypassClaim returns FairnessProvenBypasses whose count is COUNTED FROM THE DISTINCT ATTESTATIONS, never copied from the claim. Refusals: evidence absent while claimedBypasses > 0; claimedBypasses unequal to the distinct attested count; duplicate opportunityRef; an attestation whose winner is the claimant itself. UNKNOWN: an attestation with observationRef null, naming attestations[i].observationRef. Counting evidence is not policy -- no promotion, no threshold comparison, and BYPASSES_PER_LEVEL is neither imported nor referenced.

FAMILY 5 -- cap revision (fairness-evidence.ts). FairnessCapRevision {revisionRef, dimensionId, fromCapUnits, toCapUnits, drainedWorkItemIds, migrations}; FairnessCapMigration {workItemId, boundAtMost, currentBoundAtMost: number|null}. The reference's CapMigration is {ticketId, boundAtMost} with the equal-or-tighter rule stated only in a comment and enforced against reducer state, so a migration datum ALONE cannot be checked.

implementationPlan.description:
TDD RED - write packages/scheduler/src/fairness/fairness-contract.test.ts before any implementation. One test file covers all three modules; the 250-line target is a PRODUCTION-source rule and does not bind tests.

DoD 2, the three defects, each asserting the SPECIFIC stable reason code AND the refusing layer (epic rail 6 - never merely that it failed):
  (a) A BYPASS CLAIM THE CALLER CANNOT PROVE IS REFUSED, never admitted. Assert the refusal code and layer. Then assert the positive: a bypass backed by the evidence the contract requires validates. A test that only proves refusal cannot tell a working guard from a contract that refuses everything.
  (b) Rings and resource queues are REPRESENTABLE - construct a valid multi-resource ring and assert it validates, since the reference could not express one at all.
  (c) Each hostile-state gap is either closed (assert the refusal) or typed UNKNOWN WITH THE MISSING INPUT NAMED (assert the UNKNOWN carries that name). An UNKNOWN that does not say what is missing is indistinguishable from a silent pass.

DoD 3 - every refusal path is TOTAL, and the case sweep asserts it generated a NON-ZERO number of cases. Assert the count explicitly; an emptied sweep must fail rather than pass silently.

DoD 4, the boundary test that keeps this task honest: assert NO exported function decides rotation order, deficit accounting or aging. Implement it as a real property over the module's exports - enumerate them and assert each is a type guard, validator or frozen constant - not as a comment. Contracts describe and validate; scheduling belongs to task-10cab3e5.

Assert results by whole-object equality on { code, layer } rather than a .length or truthiness check, so a swapped or extra issue fails.
implementationPlan.note:
TDD RED confirmed before any implementation existed:

  npx vitest run --root . packages/scheduler/src/fairness
  FAIL packages/scheduler/src/fairness/fairness-contract.test.ts
  Error: Cannot find module './fairness-contract.js' imported from .../fairness-contract.test.ts
  Test Files 1 failed (1) | Tests no tests

WHAT THE FILE ASSERTS, mapped to the DoD items.

DoD 2(a), defect closed with a positive twin so the guard is distinguishable from a contract that refuses everything: no-evidence claim -> REFUSED FAIRNESS_CONTRACT_BYPASS_EVIDENCE_MISSING / OPPORTUNITY_EVIDENCE; unproven count -> BYPASS_COUNT_UNPROVEN; self-attested -> BYPASS_SELF_ATTESTED; and a PROVEN claim ACCEPTS, with provenBypasses whole-object-equal to 2 and opportunityRefs derived from the attestations. If the implementation copied claimedBypasses instead of counting evidence, the accept case still passes but the count-unproven case cannot, so both directions are pinned.

DoD 2(b): a valid two-resource ring with two queues ACCEPTS (the reference cannot express one at all), plus the four structural refusals -- UNDECLARED_RESOURCE, ITEM_IN_MULTIPLE_QUEUES, EMPTY_RESOURCE_SET, and a delegated malformed resource that must name layer RESOURCE rather than RING. That last one is the rail-6 "which layer refused" assertion made concrete: two layers can refuse a ring and the test pins which.

DoD 2(c): three UNKNOWN paths, each asserting the missing input BY NAME -- "dispatchability.observationRef", "attestations[0].observationRef", "migrations[0].currentBoundAtMost". Plus the identity gap closed as a refusal: a zero-width-joiner id is REFUSED with INVALID_IDENTITY, written as String.fromCharCode(0x200d) so the character is visible to a reviewer instead of being an invisible byte in the source.

DoD 3, totality with non-vacuous sweeps: 12 hostile shapes (null, undefined, string, number, boolean, symbol, array, proxy, throwing accessor, symbol-keyed record, class instance, null-prototype record) x 5 record validators = 60 cases, plus 11 for the list validator, each asserting whole-object equality on [{code, layer}] and that the validator ANSWERED rather than threw. Counts are asserted twice: toBeGreaterThan(0) AND a hand-written exact literal (12 / 60 / 11 / 34), so an emptied sweep reddens on the count test even before the per-case tests disappear.

REASON-CODE REACHABILITY: a 34-entry hand-written table of (label, thunk, disposition, code, layer, missingInput). Three closing assertions make it non-vacuous: the covered code set must EQUAL the frozen FAIRNESS_CONTRACT_ISSUE_CODES (so an unreachable declared code and an undeclared emitted code both go red), the covered layer set must equal FAIRNESS_CONTRACT_LAYERS, and missingInput must be non-null exactly when the disposition is UNKNOWN.

DoD 4, no authority, as a real property over runtime exports rather than a comment. Four parts: (1) per-module export count is non-zero AND equals a hand-written literal; (2) every runtime export is either a frozen constant or a function classified by /^validate[A-Z]/, /^is[A-Z]/, or a hand-written 3-name constructor allowlist; (3) no export name matches /next|order|sort|rotat|select|charge|promot|rank|decid|pick|schedul/i; (4) BEHAVIOURAL, not name-based -- validateRing must preserve caller order verbatim (resources given as res-b,res-a stay res-b,res-a) and pass deficit counters through unchanged, so an implementation that sorted or charged would redden even if its export names looked innocent. Two more assert accepted values are deeply frozen and that later caller mutation of the input cannot change an accepted value.

Every hostile fixture is ONE mutation off a valid base (workItem()/ring()/claim()/revision() spread helpers), per mem:refusal-test-answered-by-earlier-guard: a fixture that is invalid at an earlier layer would be answered by that layer's code and the test would pass while never reaching its subject.

Design note recorded for step 4-6: validators return exactly ONE issue, the first violation in a documented field order. That makes toEqual([{code,layer}]) deterministic and forces the implementation to have a defined check order; accumulation order would be a presentation policy the contracts have no business owning.

implementationPlan.description:
GREEN 1 - packages/scheduler/src/fairness/fairness-contract.ts plus its sibling fairness-contract.js bridge.

Holds the SHARED frozen vocabularies every other module imports - the stable reason codes and the refusing-layer set - and the WorkItem family.

Define the layer vocabulary as a frozen closed union in this module; every refusal anywhere in the fairness contracts names one of its members, so a reader can always tell WHICH layer refused. Epic rail 6 requires exactly that where more than one layer can refuse.

DO NOT reuse the reference's FairnessReasonCode union wholesale. Take the members the gap analysis justifies, and add the ones the reference could not express because it had no rings, no resource queues and no provable bypass. Every code you add must be reachable from a real refusal path that step 3's tests exercise - an unreachable code is a vocabulary claim with nothing behind it.

WorkItem is IMMUTABLE: readonly fields, frozen arrays, no setters, no mutation helpers. Its validator is TOTAL - every input shape returns either a typed OK or a typed refusal naming code and layer. No throw, no undefined return, no optimistic default.

Do NOT change fairness constants, and do NOT introduce one. If a contract appears to require a constant that does not exist, STOP and report_blocked naming it - the rail is explicit that constants are a product decision.

Target <=250 physical lines measured with `grep -c ''` (PowerShell Measure-Object -Line skips blank lines and reports headroom you do not have); split before 400.

GREEN 2 - packages/scheduler/src/fairness/fairness-ring.ts plus its .js bridge. The RING and RESOURCE families, together because a WDRR ring holds per-resource queues and separating them forces a circular import.

This is the family the reference could not express AT ALL - `grep -rn 'ring|Ring|resourceQueue|ResourceQueue|WDRR|deficit'` over packages/testkit/src/scheduler-fairness returns nothing outside tests. There is nothing to copy; design it from the gap and justify the shape.

Express STRUCTURE ONLY, never policy. The contract must be able to DESCRIBE a ring - its resources, its queues, its per-item deficit counters as DATA - and VALIDATE that a given ring is well-formed. It must NOT decide whose turn it is, must not compute a deficit increment, and must not order anything. That line is DoD 4 and it is the easiest one in this task to cross by accident: a function named `nextInRing` or `chargeDeficit` has already crossed it.

Validate the structural invariants a ring must satisfy regardless of policy: every queued item names a resource the ring declares; no item appears in two queues; counters are non-negative safe integers; the resource set is non-empty when any queue is non-empty. Each violation refuses with its own code and layer.

Immutable and frozen throughout. Total validators. <=250 lines target, split before 400.

GREEN 3 - packages/scheduler/src/fairness/fairness-evidence.ts plus its .js bridge. The OPPORTUNITY-EVIDENCE and CAP-REVISION families.

OPPORTUNITY-EVIDENCE is where defect (a) is closed BY CONSTRUCTION. The reference decodes a caller's `bypassesInLevel` and range-checks it; the production contract must make an unprovable bypass claim UNREPRESENTABLE or REFUSED.
